gen-gf-syne-tactile-fs-paquito: Paquito reads as a text serif with a confident, friendly stance. Syne Tactile is the showpiece, its broad-nib strokes never quite curling shut, while Paquito does the steadier work of carrying words without fuss.
gen-gf-tagesschrift-fs-rowan: Tagesschrift looks like glass tubing bent into letters, flat and bold. Rowan follows with a classic serif's mild, friendly contrast, its curves open enough that a longer passage moves along gently.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-amulya: Every line in Tapestry has the weight of a technical drawing pen, yet it still feels hand-made. Amulya's generous curve gaps and light touch give that looseness a modern, tidy partner.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-bespoke-sans: Tapestry draws its letters with a marker-like constant line, relaxed and personal. Bespoke Sans, a sharp sans-serif with generous room between curve ends and stems, would keep a longer passage crisp and light.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-literata: One pen tip seems to have drawn all of Tapestry. Literata offsets that with a steady, mellow modulation and wide-mouthed curves, giving the pair a bookish depth beside the hand-drawn charm.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-neco: Neco reads as a dignified text serif, with a measured swell from hairline to stem and curves that never pinch shut. Tapestry is best at cord-like curves as heavy as its stems, while Neco is best when the voice needs authority.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-plein: Reliable and clean, Plein opens a clear channel into each round letter, while Tapestry hums along in a flat gray line of constant weight. And the strongest thing here is how that loose handwriting sits against such tidy, dependable sans text.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-recia: Neon-tube strokes, loose and glowing, mark Tapestry out at once. But Recia, a classic serif with quiet variation inside each letter and generous openings, gives the pairing an authoritative footing that is better saved for brief lines.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-rowan: Rowan reads literary and friendly, a classic serif with generous curves and a mid-level stroke contrast. And what makes the pair work is Tapestry's bowls with no thinning at the sides, set against Rowan's gentler thick and thin.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans reads contemporary and approachable, with wide gaps by the stems and strokes of identical weight. Tapestry's hand-drawn warmth sits above it, so a longer passage would feel loose at the top and tidy below.
